cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, just finished tearing down idol altars from the temple all the way to Bethel (2 Kings 23:4-20). Demolition crew, CLOCK OUT. Now he gives all the people a command straight out of the Book of the Covenant.

cards.question: Josiah tells all the people to keep a feast of the LORD their God, just as it's written in the Book of the Covenant. Which feast?

cards.text: Then the writer stops the story to tell you something about this Passover. And friend, it covers a LOT of history.

cards.question: How far back would you have to go to find a Passover like Josiah's?
Josiah's Passover is kept to the LORD in Jerusalem, in the eighteenth year of his reign.

cards.text: And Josiah's not done cleaning house. There's still stuff out in plain sight across the land, and he goes after it like I go after the last chocolate chip at the bottom of the bag.

cards.question: What else does Josiah clear out of Judah and Jerusalem?
Josiah clears all of it out to carry out the words of the ___ written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the writer steps back and sizes Josiah up against every king. Before him AND after him. Friend, that is a TOUGH room.

cards.question: Of all the kings before Josiah and after him, there was no king like Josiah.
Josiah turned to the LORD with all his heart, soul and strength, according to all the Law of ___.

cards.text: Josiah just got the best review of any king, before or after. But the LORD's burning anger had been kindled against Judah. So what happens to it now? I'm leaning in like I'm watching a batch through the oven window.

cards.question: After everything Josiah did, the LORD turns away from His burning anger against Judah.
The LORD's anger burns against Judah because of all that ___, a king of Judah before Josiah (2 Kings 21:1), had done to provoke Him.

cards.text: And this doesn't come out of nowhere. The writer tells us the LORD had already said what He would do.

cards.question: What had the LORD said He would do with Judah?

answers.text: Remove Judah from His sight as He did Israel
Send a famine on Judah for seven years
Hold back the rain from Judah for years

cards.question: The LORD had said He would still keep Jerusalem, the city He chose, and the temple where He said His Name would be.

cards.text: The writer says the rest of Josiah's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Then the story picks up: during Josiah's reign, Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt marches up to help the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River.

cards.question: Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt is marching up toward the Euphrates. What does King Josiah do?

answers.text: Sends him a gift of gold

cards.question: King Josiah comes home alive from his face-off with Pharaoh Neco.
Pharaoh Neco faced King Josiah and killed him at ___.

cards.text: Josiah's servants carry his body in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and bury him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land need a new king.

cards.question: Who do the people of the land anoint and make king in Josiah's place?

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then the writer steps back and sizes Josiah up against every king." / "Before him AND after him." / "Friend, that is a TOUGH room." It isn't the opening card, so the limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences. It isn't the passage's opening card, and even the opening card is capped at three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens with "Josiah just got the best review of any king, before or after," which retells 2 Kings 23:25. It only cites 2 Kings 23:26. That line is also a recap of the card the baker just answered. Either cut the recap or cite 2 Kings 23:25-26.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question "How far back would you have to go to find a Passover like Josiah's?" assumes a Passover like Josiah's was kept in the days of the judges. 2 Kings 23:22 only says no such Passover had been kept from the days of the judges through the kings. It never says one was kept in the judges' time. Reword to match the verse, for example: "No Passover like this had been kept since the days of whom?"

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "It covers a LOT of history" points away from "The days of King Hezekiah." Hezekiah reigned only a few generations before Josiah, so the setup rules that wrong answer out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Only the right answer is a son of Josiah. The wrong answers are Amon, Josiah's own father, and Hezekiah, his great-grandfather. Neither could take Josiah's place, so the right answer stands out and a baker can rule out the others without reasoning from the passage.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Story cards 4, 7 and 11 are plain reporting with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 7 in particular just lists the record book and Neco's march. The serious moment of Josiah's death can stay respectful, but these cards read as stripped down.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
